related_questions.question: What caused the black vomit?
related_questions.snippet: The color of your vomit can be a sign of a serious health condition. Black or brown vomit can be a sign of internal bleeding. This type of vomit is also often called “coffee ground vomitus” as the partially digested blood looks like coffee grounds and is caused by bleeding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.

related_questions.question: Can liver disease cause black vomit?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, liver disease, particularly cirrhosis and its complications like esophageal varices, can cause black vomit. This happens when there's bleeding in the upper gastrointestinal (GI) tract, often due to ruptured varices, which are enlarged blood vessels in the esophagus. The blood, after being partially digested in the stomach, turns black, creating the appearance of "coffee grounds" or a dark, tarry substance in the vomit.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, liver disease, particularly cirrhosis and its complications like esophageal varices, can cause black vomit

list.title: Liver Cirrhosis and Portal Hypertension:
list.snippet: Cirrhosis, a condition where healthy liver tissue is replaced by scar tissue, can lead to portal hypertension, an increase in blood pressure in the portal vein. This increased pressure can cause blood vessels in the esophagus (esophageal varices) to become enlarged and fragile.

list.title: Bleeding Varices:
list.snippet: These enlarged veins can rupture and bleed, causing blood to enter the GI tract. The blood can then be vomited up, and if it has been in the stomach for a while, it will be digested and turn black.

list.title: Other Causes:
list.snippet: While esophageal varices are a common cause of black vomit in liver disease, other conditions like gastritis, gastric ulcers, and even certain medications can also cause GI bleeding and black vomit.

list.title: Important Note:
list.snippet: Vomiting blood, especially if it's black or looks like coffee grounds, is a serious symptom that requires immediate medical attention, according to the Liver Foundation.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, liver disease, particularly cirrhosis, can lead to bleeding in the upper GI tract, which can cause black vomit due to the digestion and oxidation of blood. If you experience black vomit, seek immediate medical help.

snippet_highlighted_words: internal bleeding, usually in the upper gastrointestinal (GI) tract

text_blocks.snippet: Possible causes of black vomit include:

list.snippet: Peptic ulcers: Ulcers in the stomach or duodenum can bleed, and the blood can be vomited up as black, coffee-ground-like material.
Esophageal varices: Swollen and bleeding veins in the esophagus can also cause black vomit.
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining can lead to bleeding and subsequent black vomit.
Mallory-Weiss tears: Tears in the lining of the esophagus, often caused by forceful vomiting, can also result in bleeding and black vomit.
Stomach cancer or esophageal cancer: In rare cases, black vomit can be a symptom of these cancers.
Viral hemorrhagic fevers: Some viral infections, like Ebola, can cause internal bleeding and black vomit.
Other GI bleeding: Any source of bleeding in the upper GI tract can potentially lead to black vomit.

text_blocks.snippet: Important note: Vomiting blood, whether it's bright red or black, is a serious symptom that requires immediate medical attention. If you or someone you know is vomiting blood, seek emergency medical care.
